wins: Mapped perimeter services rapidly, discovering HTTP (port 80) and SSH (port 22) with consistent banners that enriched situational awareness.
Captured HTTP response headers that revealed a vulnerable CMS version, enabling clear articulation of next exploit vectors.
Documented credential brute force attempts which, while unsuccessful, confirmed account lockout behavior and refined pivot assumptions.
fails: Unable to achieve initial foothold; SSH brute forcing stalled because rate limiting prevented password spraying before timeout.
Privilege escalation stalled after default web shell upload failed to execute due to missing write permissions on /var/www.
Total run failed to reach objective within allotted time, highlighted by zero success rate despite high reconnaissance throughput.
key_outcomes.summary: Reckoned a well-instrumented reconnaissance phase with clear artifact collection but lacked successful exploitation and pivoting; focus next on tailored exploits and persistence bypasses.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: SSH password spraying hits lockout before exhaustion of common credentials due to aggressive rate limits.
Uploaded web shell unable to execute because /var/www directory enforces strict ownership, preventing privilege escalation.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner indicates OpenSSH 8.x
skill_cards.then_action: Run nmap ssh-auth-methods and ssh-brute scripts to characterize authentication restrictions, then adjust timing options

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service exposes a CMS and robots.txt reveals runnable endpoints
skill_cards.then_action: Execute nikto and gobuster with aggressive wordlists plus HTTP header inspection to confirm CMS version and potential RCE paths

skill_cards.if_condition: When default web upload fails to execute
skill_cards.then_action: Switch to writing a PHP reverse shell via curl/wget to tmp and execute through low-privilege cron/job to bypass ownership restrictions

memory_ops.reason: SSH enumeration produced rich telemetry despite failed bruteforce, enabling adjusted timing assumptions.

next_experiments.title: Time-aware SSH brute force
next_experiments.description: Implement ssh-brute with --max-retries 2 and --scan-delay 5s to respect lockouts while cycling through candidate passwords from rockyou subset.

next_experiments.title: CMS-specific exploitation
next_experiments.description: Identify CMS plugins from HTTP responses, download matching exploit from ExploitDB, and attempt authenticated SSRF or RCE via POST to vulnerable endpoint.

next_experiments.title: Temporal web shell persistence
next_experiments.description: Upload PHP reverse shell to /tmp, then trigger via cronjob entry or log poisoning that executes under www-data to bypass /var/www restrictions.
